name: Kereho
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard & Antonia Soriente. 2015. The languages and peoples of the Müller Mountains: A contribution to the study of the origins of Borneo's nomads and their languages. Wacana 16(2): 339-354. doi:10.17510/wacana.v16i2.381
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: First-hand Kereho data (Sellato): p.346 Table 2 'Kerého consonants (Uhéng and Busang)' (no /j w g/, [β] for medial /b/, Kereho Busang has preploded final nasals), Table 6 gives 6 (Uheng) / 7 (Busang) vowels. Nothing on Kereho stress; the paper's only stress remark (p.344) concerns Seputan ('strong stress on the penultimate syllable', vs Aoheng).

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Mānoa. 723 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Own Kereho fieldwork (consultant Pietrus, Kereho town, Keriau R.). Sec. 2.5 Müller-Schwaner (pp.127-139) is historical phonology only; Appendix 4 (p.516ff) Kereho wordlist has sporadic, unexplained acute accents on 28 of 99 rows (mostly penultimate: koráho, kotólaʔ, tohókan, poŋánon; a few final: panó, suŋé, sapéʔ). No statement about Kereho stress anywhere; transcription conventions (sec. 1.5) do not explain the accents.
